kurz: Which assets can be sold tax-free after a holding period of one year, and when the exemption threshold applies within the period.

bloecke.md:
So far, this module has almost always been about Section 20 EStG (Income Tax Act). There, the bank settles the tax, 25% plus solidarity surcharge applies, and the holding period plays no role. This does not apply to Bitcoin, a gold bar, a watch or a non-interest-bearing dollar balance. For tax purposes, each of these falls into the category of **other assets (andere Wirtschaftsgüter)** and therefore comes under Section 23 EStG, the provision on private disposal transactions (private Veräußerungsgeschäfte).

A second set of rules applies to these assets, which in several respects provides for the opposite of Section 20 EStG. Tax is levied at the personal marginal tax rate instead of a flat 25%, so at up to 45%. In return, there is a holding period of a kind that has not existed for shares since 2009. Once it has expired, the gain is completely tax-free, regardless of its size. In addition, no bank withholds tax; declaring it is the investor's responsibility.

bloecke.unter: The classification of the asset determines the tax rate, the holding period and loss offsetting; the outward form of the product plays no role.

bloecke.md:
## Holding period and exemption threshold

The period under Section 23(1) sentence 1 no. 2 EStG is one year and is calculated to the day. What counts are the contractual transactions, that is, purchase and sale, not delivery or crediting. Where several purchases of amounts of the same foreign currency are made, sentence 3 of the same provision prescribes the first in, first out sequence. For crypto assets, the tax authorities apply this sequence to the holding period if the units sold cannot be allocated individually (BMF circular of 6 March 2025). Unlike in a securities account, however, nobody keeps the books here; the allocation has to come from your own records.

The exemption threshold (Freigrenze) is €1,000 (Section 23(3) sentence 5 EStG, raised from €600 with effect from the 2024 assessment period). It applies to all private disposal transactions in a calendar year taken together. Crypto, gold, collector's items, foreign currencies and also a property within the ten-year period share the same amount. With joint assessment, each spouse is entitled to the exemption threshold for their own transactions. An amount one spouse does not use up cannot be used by the other.

With a total gain of €999.99, everything remains tax-free. At €1,000.00, the entire amount becomes taxable, not just the part above the threshold. At a marginal tax rate of 42%, the last cent of gain therefore raises the tax from zero to €420. This is one of the few cases in which it can make arithmetical sense to postpone realising a gain to the following year.

bloecke.md:
## Taxation of crypto assets

Since the judgment of the Federal Fiscal Court (BFH) of 14 February 2023 (IX R 3/22), it has been settled at the highest judicial level that Bitcoin and Ether fall under Section 23 EStG. According to this ruling, cryptocurrencies are other assets. The court saw no structural enforcement deficit that would make the taxation unconstitutional. The position of the tax authorities is set out in the BMF circular of 6 March 2025. It replaces the circular of 10 May 2022 and additionally governs the duties to cooperate and to keep records.

For tax purposes, every transaction in which coins change hands in return for consideration counts as a disposal and at the same time as an acquisition of what is received. Gifts and inheritances do not count. Disposals occur, for example, in these cases:

- When Bitcoin is exchanged for Ether, the Bitcoin is disposed of at the price on the day of the exchange and the Ether is acquired, for which a new one-year period begins.
- Paying with crypto assets is a disposal at the price at the time of payment, even for small amounts.
- A detour via a stablecoin changes nothing, because the stablecoin is also an asset in its own right.

Ongoing income from staking or lending belongs to other income (sonstige Einkünfte) under Section 22 no. 3 EStG and not to private disposal transactions. A separate exemption threshold of €256 a year applies to it. The valuation is made at the time of receipt. From then on, the coins received have their own acquisition date and their own one-year period.

The most widespread concern relates to the period under Section 23(1) sentence 1 no. 2 sentence 4 EStG. It is extended to ten years if income is earned from an asset. The tax authorities expressly do not apply this extension to crypto assets, so staked coins are tax-free after one year.

Even though no bank withholds capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer), the tax authorities learn about the transactions. With the implementation of the EU directive DAC8, crypto-asset service providers report their users and their transactions to the tax authorities from reporting year 2026. The matching is automated. Investors who have not declared anything for past years can put this right through a correction under Section 153 AO (Fiscal Code) or a voluntary disclosure (Selbstanzeige) under Section 371 AO. The limitation period for assessment is normally four years, and ten years in the case of tax evasion (Section 169(2) AO). It begins at the end of the year in which the return is filed, but at the latest at the end of the third year after the year in which the tax arose (Section 170(2) sentence 1 no. 1 AO).

## Physical and securitised gold

Physical gold is treated like any other asset. A sale within one year is taxable at the personal rate; after that, it is tax-free. In addition, on purchase, investment gold is exempt from VAT under Section 25c UStG (VAT Act). This does not apply to silver, platinum and palladium, which are subject to 19% VAT. For imported silver coins, this burden is reduced by margin taxation (Differenzbesteuerung) under Section 25a UStG.

For securitised gold, the Federal Fiscal Court ruled in its judgment of 12 May 2015 (VIII R 4/15) that the Xetra-Gold bearer bond is treated like physical gold despite its form as a security and does not fall under Section 20 EStG. The court based this on the securitised claim to delivery of the metal. After one year, the gain is tax-free. The same applies to products with a comparable structure such as Euwax Gold II.

If this delivery claim is missing, the product counts as a capital claim of another kind (sonstige Kapitalforderung) within the meaning of Section 20(1) no. 7 EStG, whose sale is taxed under Section 20(2) sentence 1 no. 7 EStG. Then 26.375% applies, without partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) and without a holding period. This group includes many gold ETCs issued abroad, which look like an equivalent alternative in the portfolio. Whether a foreign ETC with a delivery claim is treated in the same way as Xetra-Gold has not been uniformly settled. The custodian bank initially deducts tax according to its own classification; any correction is made via the tax return.

bloecke.md:
## Collector's items and foreign currency

The same one-year period and the same personal tax rate apply to art, classic cars, wines, watches and collector's coins. Two special features must be noted. If income is earned with the item, for example by renting a painting out to a company, Section 23(1) sentence 1 no. 2 sentence 4 EStG extends the period to ten years. In addition, sentence 2 of the same provision rules out deducting losses on **items of everyday use (Gegenstände des täglichen Gebrauchs)** from the outset. The loss from selling a used car has no tax effect, whereas the gain from selling a classic car is taxed.

Foreign currency balances are regularly overlooked. For tax purposes, a non-interest-bearing dollar account with a broker counts as an asset and not as money. Every conversion back into euros within one year realises the currency gain under Section 23 EStG. This applies even if no euros flow at all. When a security is bought from the dollar balance, the balance is used up and the currency gain is thereby realised, separately from and at a different time than the later gain on the security itself. If the balance earns interest, however, the tax authorities allocate the currency gain to capital income under Section 20(2) sentence 1 no. 7 EStG, without a holding period (BMF circular of 14 May 2025, para. 131). With brokers that settle every order in euros immediately, no balance arises at all, so the question does not come up there.

Losses from private disposal transactions may only be offset against gains of the same kind (Section 23(3) sentence 7 EStG). A carryback to the previous year and an unlimited carryforward are possible (sentence 8). Offsetting against the share and capital loss pots of Section 20 EStG, by contrast, is not possible in either direction. A crypto loss of €10,000 therefore does not reduce the flat-rate withholding tax on dividends by a single cent. The carryforward must be determined separately, so the losses must also be declared in years without gains.

The one-year period only applies in the private sphere. Investors who buy and sell systematically, act for third parties, build up inventories and present themselves on the market become commercial traders under Section 15 EStG. Trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) is then due, VAT questions arise, and no holding period applies. There are no fixed numerical limits. The courts look at the overall picture, that is, the number and frequency of transactions, the use of borrowed money and the investor's own presence on the market. According to the tax authorities, holding and selling your own holdings, including staking in your own name, as a rule remains private asset management.

There is no tax certificate for Section 23. The declaration is made on the **other income annex (Anlage SO)**, in which crypto assets have had their own lines since 2023. Only what is documented will stand up. This includes the complete transaction history for each exchange and wallet, the price at the time of each transaction and the fees as incidental acquisition costs. The BMF circular of 6 March 2025 expressly requires records that can be traced. Where there are gaps, the tax office may estimate, and an estimate rarely turns out in the taxpayer's favour.

mitnehmen: The legal structure of an asset determines the tax, which is why gold in a safe and gold as an ETC without a delivery claim are treated completely differently.

After a holding period of one year, gains from crypto, gold, collector's items and foreign currencies are completely tax-free; within the period, the personal marginal tax rate applies instead of the flat-rate withholding tax.

The €1,000 under Section 23(3) sentence 5 EStG is an exemption threshold for all private disposal transactions in a year taken together, and at a total gain of exactly €1,000 the entire gain is already taxable.
Exchanges, payments and buying a security from a foreign currency balance are disposals, even if no euro appears in the account.
Losses under Section 23 are offset separately and can never reduce capital income.

begriffe.text: Sale of an asset from private wealth within the holding period under Section 23 EStG, which is one year for movable assets and ten years for land. It is taxed at the personal marginal tax rate, and not at all once the period has expired.

Limit above which the entire amount becomes taxable, not just the excess. Under Section 23 EStG, the gain only remains tax-free if it is less than €1,000 per person and year; for other income under Section 22 no. 3 EStG, if it is less than €256.
Gold in the form of bars or coins with a legally defined minimum fineness. Transactions in it are exempt from VAT under Section 25c UStG, unlike silver, platinum and palladium.
